name: FlexLayout (Yoga flexbox)
baseline: UIStackView (and Auto Layout) laying out self-sizing UICollectionView cells
verdict_reason: FlexLayout still beats UIStackView and matches manual frame code, but the README's 8x-12x figure is from iPhone 5S to X on iOS 11. Current runs of the same benchmark show 3.8x (iPhone 16) and 4.1x (iPhone 13 Pro, iOS 18.6) over UIStackView.
tier_reason: Public LayoutFrameworkBenchmark app with per-device raw data, device and iOS version stated, Release mode; maintained by the FlexLayout authors.
claimed_speedup: README: 'between 8x and 12x faster than UIStackViews' (iPhone 5S to X). Current data, 100 cells: iPhone 16 0.019 s vs 0.0728 s UIStackView (3.8x, derived from page data) and 0.0595 s Auto Layout (3.1x, derived from page data); iPhone 13 Pro iOS 18.6 0.0192 s vs 0.0786 s UIStackView (4.1x, derived from page data) and 0.064 s Auto Layout (3.3x, derived from page data); manual frame layout 0.0208 s and 0.0216 s.
workload: Lay out a feed-style UICollectionView cell for 10 to 100 cells per pass; seconds for vc.view.layoutIfNeeded() on the main thread.
hardware: iPhone 16; iPhone 13 Pro; older runs on iPhone 5S to XS
os: iOS 18.6 (iPhone 13 Pro); iPhone 16 OS not stated; iOS 11 to 12 for older runs
toolchain: Release mode per benchmark README; exact Swift version not stated
one_liner: Swift wrapper over Meta's Yoga flexbox engine; about 4x faster than UIStackView on current iPhones in LayoutFrameworkBenchmark.
how_it_is_fast: FlexLayout hands layout to Yoga, a C++ flexbox implementation that computes frames in a single tree pass and caches measurements. UIStackView is built on Auto Layout, so every arranged subview adds constraints to the engine. Yoga avoids constraint solving altogether and writes frames directly.
use_it_when: Screens built from nested UIStackViews that show up in Time Profiler, especially inside scrolling cells
Teams that already think in CSS flexbox or share layout logic with React Native
skip_it_when: Simple screens where UIStackView cost is not measurable
Projects that cannot take a C++ dependency
caveats: The 8x-12x figure is from 2017-2018 devices on iOS 11; current devices show 3.8x-4.1x over UIStackView.
The benchmark is maintained by the same authors as FlexLayout.
The iPhone 16 sheet labels the row 'FlexLayout 1.3' while the iPhone 13 Pro sheet says 'FlexLayout 2.2', so the version actually run on iPhone 16 is unclear.
Yoga itself is not benchmarked directly; the README says only the FlexLayout wrapper was measured.
tradeoffs: Layout is described in a flexbox DSL rather than constraints; no Interface Builder support.

evidence.quote: FlexLayout and PinLayout are **between 8x and 12x faster than UIStackViews**, and this for all types of iPhone (5S/6/6S/7/8/X)
